title: Almudevar & Almudevar (2026): Reproducibility and Statistical Methodology
materials: arXiv HTML rendering read through a fetch tool: abstract, section list, Tables 1 and 4, and quoted passages of Sections 2.1-2.2, 3.5, 3.6, 5. PDF not downloadable here (shell egress 403). Per-study OSC p-values and replication sample sizes behind the type II error figure not in hand. Cited sources (Nosek 2015, Klein 2014, Camerer 2016) not read.
decision_context: Whether to read the Open Science Collaboration's 36% replication rate (Nosek et al. 2015) as an estimate of how many published psychology findings are true, or as largely an artifact of how the replications were powered. Assessor-chosen paper; no decision owner named.

claims.text: We show that the OSC methodology induces a bias that is able by itself to explain the discrepancy between the OSC estimates of reproducibility and other more optimistic estimates made by similar studies.
claims.evidence_location: Abstract; mechanism Sections 3.3-3.5; fit Table 4 and Section 3.5
claims.measurand: observed replication rate PPV_obs, predicted from prevalence pi and replication type II error beta*
claims.falsifiers: An independent estimate of pi for the OSC originals inside 0.018-0.048 (fits OSC with OSC's reported beta* 0.08, R6) and outside 0.043-0.255 (the range the corrected beta* needs). A high-power re-replication of the same OSC items whose success rate stays near 0.36. Neither run in the paper.
claims.label: DERIVED
claims.instrument: eq. 3 with pi = 0.25 (main) and 0.05 (interactions) and mean beta* 0.468

claims.text: the mean type II error is now 0.468, considerably higher than the average 0.08 reported by the OSC-RP
claims.measurand: mean conditional type II error of the OSC replications, with effect size re-estimated by MLE from each original p-value
claims.falsifiers: Recomputing from OSC's per-study p-values and replication sample sizes gives a mean near 0.08. Not recomputed here: inputs not in hand.
claims.label: DERIVED

claims.falsifiers: Table 4 counts differ from the OSC data file (not checked: OSC file not read). Arithmetic recomputed: totals 35/97 and Fisher p 0.0228 (R2, R3).

tools.output: Type THEORETICAL (model, derivation, review). Defaults 00/01/04/06. Overrides: 02, because the fit rests on an imposed quantity (pi); 03, because the 'more optimistic' studies are used as agreement. Toolkit fit: no type covers a re-analysis of other studies' published data; THEORETICAL plus overrides used.

8 claims, verbatim. C1 in conditional form: IF pi for the OSC originals is about 0.25 (0.05 for interactions) AND mean beta* is about 0.468, THEN 35/97 is the expected rate. Both antecedents carry the result; neither is observed.

pi graded IMPOSED: 'Suppose' and 'conjecture' (Section 3.5), with a reason given for each value but no measurement. beta* 0.468 is derived from inputs not in hand (per-study p-values, replication n), so UNDECLARED here rather than checked. Toolkit fit: the measurement grades have no value for 'computed, not recomputed'; UNDECLARED was the nearest.

ML-RP vs model: SHARED_UPSTREAM. pi = 0.25 is set from ML-RP (Table 1 label; 11/13 implies pi 0.234, R7), then ML-RP's closeness to 0.857 is reported in Section 3.6. Camerer vs model: independent data, but at n = 18 compatible with both the bias reading (0.486) and the no-bias reading (0.796), R8. Toolkit fit: 'calibration reused as confirmation' has no route of its own; SHARED_UPSTREAM fits loosely.

Open branches for OSC's 35/97: (a) protocol bias, inflated original effects leading to underpowered replications (paper); (b) low prevalence, pi about 0.03 with OSC's reported beta*, no bias needed (R6); (c) a mixture of (a) and (b); (d) other moderators of replication (Gilbert et al. 2016 is cited, not modelled). The observed rate alone does not separate (a) from (b). Cheapest discriminator: re-replicate a sample of the same OSC items powered on bias-corrected effect sizes. Under (a) success rises toward PPV; under (b) it stays low. Not run in the paper.

Term frame: 'reproducibility' in OSC carries several indicators (significance 36%, CI containment 47%, subjective 39%; Introduction). The paper's model is about significance only. 'Explain the discrepancy' applies to that one indicator. Observer-position and lower-layer checks: NOT_APPLICABLE to this material.

Target: is OSC's low rate mostly an artifact of the replication protocol? Rendering: 'able by itself to explain'. That shows sufficiency under an imposed pi, not that the artifact is the explanation. Arithmetic recomputed (recompute.py R1-R8): the predictions in Sections 3.5 and 3.6 reproduce exactly.

decisions.text: Read OSC's 36% as an estimate of the share of published psychology findings that would replicate under adequate power? If pi is near 0.25, this paper says no (the protocol depresses the rate). If pi is near 0.03, the rate stands without any bias. pi is not measured.

Treat this paper as having shown that the OSC rate is a methodological artifact? It shows that the artifact is sufficient under assumed prevalences, and that the same arithmetic reproduces OSC and Camerer. It does not separate that from a low-prevalence reading (R6, R8).

Adopt the power-analysis point (do not power replications on original effect estimates, which overestimate effects after selection on significance; Sections 3.3-3.4) when planning replications. This does not depend on the value of pi.

design_checks.finding: The prevalence used for OSC (pi = 0.25) is labelled 'consistent with ML-RP' (Table 1); Klein et al. 2014 studied a hand-picked set of effects. Selection of that set is not discussed as a reason it may differ from OSC's sample.

The model treats 'replicated' as a significant same-direction replication (35/97). OSC also reported CI containment (47%) and subjective success (39%) (Introduction); the model addresses only the significance criterion.
Intervals are given for observed rates (35/97; 11/18, recomputed R4). No interval is given for the mean type II error 0.468 or for pi; the predicted rates in Section 3.5 are point values.
Two subsets (main effects, interactions) are fitted with two separately chosen prevalences (0.25, 0.05; Section 3.5). One free parameter per observed rate.

Type II error computed on N = 93 of 97 after bounding effect estimates below by 0 (Section 3.5); 'a number of P-values were given as 0' (Section 3.5, stated limitation). 11 studies outside the main-effect and interaction rows (4/11 replicated, R2) are not discussed.

The main-effect vs interaction split (23/49 vs 8/37, Fisher p 0.0228, R3) is attributed to prevalence. Whether effect type covaries with sub-field or original sample size is not examined in the passages read.
Model and re-analysis paper; no preregistration stated or expected.
